page.layout: One column of Hebrew-Latin dictionary entries; running head centred at top, page number at top right; catchword at right below the last line; no marginal notes.

main_text.p: מִשְׁפָּח m. Suppuratio, vel Aggregatio, Jesa.5.7. nempe Cumulatio peccati ad peccatum, ut R.Salomon explicat; Pertinacia, Contumacia; cum ש loco ס.

מִסְפְּחוֹת f.p. Confibulae, Ezech.13.18. Generale nomen, juxta quosdam, earum rerum quibus aliquid constringitur & conjungitur, ut adhæresçat; R.Davia Kimchi, Pepla; alii Tiaras: alii Cervicalia reddunt: Aff. מִסְפְּחוֹתֵיכֶם Confibulas vestras, v.21.

סִפְל m. Simpulum, Vasis genus, Jud.6.38. Chaldæus, לְקַנָּא דְמַיָּא Lagenam aquarum, vertit: בְּסִפְל In simpulo, Jud.5.25. Chald. בְּפִילִי Phiala, ex qua bibunt heroes & magnifici, ut Kimchi addit.

סָפַן Texit, Obtexit: Affine est Verbo צָפַן. Particip. Præter. סָפוּן Tectus, Protectus est, Deuter.33,21. וְסָפַן בָּאֳרֵז Et tectum erat cedrinis, 1.Regum 7.3. Plurale. בְּבָתֵּיכֶם סְפוּנִים In domibus vestris tectis, Hagg.1.v.4. Constr. & cum וּשְׁפָנֵי ש Et tecta, Occulta, Deut.33.19. Futur. וַיִּסְפֹּן Et obtexit, 1.Reg.6.9.
סְפִינָה f. Navis, proprie magna, quæ superne Tecta est, Jon.1.5.

סַף Limen, Pelvis, Crater, Zachar.12.2. Ezech. 40.6. Aff. סַפּוֹ Limen suum, Ezech.43.8. Plurale. סִפִּים Limina, Jesa.6.4. וְאֶת־הַסְּפָּים Atque etiam pelves, Jer. 52.19. Fœmin. סְפּוֹת Pelves; 2.Reg.12.13. Et cum Pathach, וּסְפּוֹת Et pelves, 2.Sam.17.28.
הִסְתּוֹפֵף Hithp. Limen frequentare, Ad limen manere, quasi Liminare dicas, Psal.84.11.

סָפַק Plaudere, Complodere: & ex usu linguæ Chaldaicæ, Sufficere, Pro ס quandoque est ש. Præter. וַיִּסְפַּק Et plaudat Moab, Jer.48.26. סְפָקָם Complodit eos, Job.34.26. סָפַקְתִּי Plausi, Jer.31.19. Imp. סְפָק

page.notes: Right-hand margin and lower part of the page carry only a blot or stain near the top right and the Google digitiser watermark, which are left out. Doubtful points: the nikud on several Hebrew forms (סִפְל, סָפַן, סִפּוֹן, סִפִּים, סְפָקָם, סָפַקְתִּי) is read from a small, blurred print and may differ in its vowel signs; the Hebrew letters are otherwise legible. The last entry ends with the catchword "Plaude" at the foot of the page.
